title: Elastic capacity failover bridge and temporary SLO softening hotpatch
author: Aditi Rao
description: Incident-driven hotpatch: during a regional capacity surge we observed sustained SLO violations caused by long-tail KV cache pressure and unexpectedly high streaming concurrency. This PR adds an "elastic capacity failover bridge"—a short-lived routing shim that gracefully spills excess in-flight requests to lower-cost compatible variants and a token-budgeted degradation path while preserving critical latencies for priority tenants. It also introduces a temporary SLO softening policy that loosens enforcement thresholds for up to 10 minutes per-region under operator control, plus a fast rollback flag and telemetry to verify customer impact. The goal is to give on-call teams a predictable, reversible mechanism to keep the control plane and high-priority customers online during capacity storms without a full rollback. Changes include runtime bridge manager, health and quota adapters, new feature-flag hooks in the console API, docs and playbook updates, tests, and a small Helm config to expose the bridge config to Dedicated clusters. This is a hotpatch targeted for immediate rollforward with canary, used only for operational mitigation; follow-up PRs will upstream a permanent policy with automated decay and tighter perf tuning.
